topFixes: Rebuild the 3D presentation first. The waxy exterior, visibly faceted organs and ragged, paper-thin cut surfaces look like a prototype beside BioDigital. Improve mesh normals, section caps, material differentiation and lighting; anatomical legibility matters more than photorealism.

Replace the translucent pile-up in selected views with deliberate isolation: keep the selected organ opaque and render only essential surrounding structures as faint silhouettes. The uterus currently remains visually entangled despite the 'on its own' message.

Constrain camera framing to the unobstructed canvas. The desktop clitoris selection balloons behind the header and inspector; each selection should fit between the controls with useful anatomical context.

Redesign callout placement with collision avoidance and noncrossing leader lines. Mobile opening labels cross, while desktop labels cluster tightly over the anatomy. Show fewer labels initially and reveal secondary structures on selection.

Unify desktop controls into a clear workspace: view navigation beside the canvas, one compact tool rail and one inspector. The current header, left panel, bottom tabs, top-right tour and inspector feel independently positioned rather than composed.

Refine the mobile selected state: replace the oversized yellow isolation banner with a compact status row, preserve an explicit active-view state and fit the selected anatomy above the bottom sheet. Too much of the remaining canvas is consumed by interface chrome.

Give the manual a more authored typographic system. Retain the strong title, but distinguish instructional headings, anatomical names, metadata and actions through a tighter size-and-weight scale; extend the figure-number and rule language instead of relying on generic white boxes.

Separate exploration from simulation. Move arousal and orgasm controls into a clearly named secondary mode, make introductory guidance specific to each view, and place rotation/zoom instructions near the canvas rather than inside the reading panel.
